title: Otro chele
desc: Somebody arrives with the notebook you used to have
setting: Tom has been in the country three months, speaks careful Spanish, and has just said tú to don Emilio.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: Le dije tú y él se dio la vuelta. ¿Hice algo mal?
steps.en: I said tú to him and he turned away. Did I do something wrong?

options.es: Aquí es vos, o usted. El tú suena a telenovela.
options.en: Here it is vos, or usted. Tú sounds like a soap opera.
options.feedback: The rule and the reason it matters, in one line he will remember.
Correct and thin. He will use vos with the boss tomorrow.

options.es: No te preocupés, ya se le pasa.
options.en: Do not worry, he will get over it.
options.feedback: He will. Tom will also do it again on Thursday.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: ¿Y cuál es la regla de cuándo va cada uno?
steps.en: And what is the rule for when each one goes?

options.es: No hay una regla. Hay como veinte y se aprenden oyendo.
options.en: There is no rule. There are about twenty and you learn them by listening.
options.feedback: Honest, and it is the answer you were given. Inventing a rule would send him in the wrong direction for a year.

options.es: A los viejos usted, a los del taller vos.
options.en: Usted to old people, vos to the workshop men.
options.feedback: A useful first approximation that will fail him in about six places.

options.es: Con el tiempo te sale solo.
options.en: With time it comes out on its own.
options.feedback: True and useless today. Give him the two he needs this week.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: Entonces el cuaderno no me sirve de nada.
steps.en: So the notebook is no use to me at all.

options.es: Sirve. A mí me sirvió. Pero lo otro se agarra estando.
options.en: It is of use. It was to me. But the rest is picked up by being here.
options.feedback: You did not take his method away from him. You put it in its place, which is what somebody did for you.
Blunt. He has three months invested in that notebook.

options.en: Throw it away. That is no use.
options.feedback: You wrote refranes in one for a month. Do not tell him that.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.en: (in December, at your gate) Thank you.

options.es: (quedarse hablando en el portón veinte minutos)
options.en: (stay talking at the gate for twenty minutes)
options.feedback: He said thank you and did not leave, which means he is waiting for the goodbye to take its proper length. You are teaching him without saying a word.

options.es: De nada. Nos vemos el lunes.
options.en: You are welcome. See you Monday.
options.feedback: Kind and quick. Quick is the one thing a Nicaraguan goodbye is not.
The right words, thirty minutes early. He will learn to leave like a foreigner.
